title: Base change of equivalences between quasicategorical isofibrations
statement:
Use quasicategories, simplicial pullbacks and functor equivalences of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and isofibrations as defined in [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-exponentiation]. Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B,\mathcal S$ be quasicategories in a common universe, let $p:\mathcal A\to\mathcal S$ and $q:\mathcal B\to\mathcal S$ be isofibrations, and let $v:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be a functor equivalence satisfying $qv=p$ as simplicial maps. For every quasicategory $\mathcal R$ and simplicial functor $h:\mathcal R\to\mathcal S$, the degreewise simplicial pullbacks are quasicategories, and the induced map
$$\mathcal R\times_{\mathcal S}\mathcal A\longrightarrow\mathcal R\times_{\mathcal S}\mathcal B$$
is an equivalence of quasicategories. No fibration hypothesis on $v$ or $h$ is imposed.

source.place: Corollary 4.5.3.34 (Kerodon Tag 03PM), with the middle and right vertical functors identities, together with pullback stability of isofibrations. Kerodon tag, not Stacks tag. Read online 2026-10-16; WANTED: archived source.

proof.text: Fix an arbitrary quasicategory $\mathcal R$ and map $h:\mathcal R\to\mathcal S$, and choose a common sufficiently large universe containing $\mathcal A,\mathcal B,\mathcal S,\mathcal R$ and these maps. Work in the Joyal model structure supplied by [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure], writing $C,F,W$ for its cofibrations, fibrations and weak equivalences. The inner-horn and source-equivalence lifting conditions defining the given isofibrations $p,q$ agree literally with clause (1) of [lem-coef-joyal-quasicategory-characterizations]. Thus $p,q\in F$. Clause (2) applied to the given coherent quasi-inverse of $v$ gives $v\in W$. All three source and target simplicial sets are quasicategories, as those characterizations require.

source.place: Theorem 3.6.1 and Corollary 3.6.6, with Theorem 3.6.8 for the test definition of W.

proof.text: We will use only the lifting characterizations in [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure] to manipulate $F$ and $F\cap W$. Any class characterized by a fixed right lifting property is closed under pullback: compose a lifting square with the pullback projection, take its filler, and pair that filler with the prescribed map to the new base. It is also closed under composition: first lift against the second map, then lift the resulting square against the first map. Every identity has each such right lifting property (its filler is the bottom map). Applying this to the right classes of $(C\cap W,F)$ and $(C,F\cap W)$ proves the pullback and composition closures we need, and shows that identities belong to $W$. These are explicit lifting-square arguments, not an assumption of right properness.

source.place: Agent proof below the derived coefficient adjunction: elementary lifting-class closure and identity calculation.

proof.text: Form the degreewise pullback $P=\mathcal A\times_{\mathcal S}\mathcal B$, with projections $\pi_A,\pi_B$, using [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. The equation $qv=p$ defines the graph $\gamma:\mathcal A\to P$, $a\mapsto(a,v(a))$, as a simplicial map. Apply the trivial-cofibration/fibration factorization of [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure] to this particular graph, obtaining $\mathcal A\xrightarrow{i}Z\xrightarrow{k}P$ with $i\in C\cap W$, $k\in F$ and $ki=\gamma$. The factorization occurs in the chosen universe. Define $r=\pi_Ak:Z\to\mathcal A$, $t=\pi_Bk:Z\to\mathcal B$, and $s=pr=qt:Z\to\mathcal S$.

source.place: Agent graph factorization over the joint endpoint base, supplying the ordinary-pullback foundation for proof paragraph 2.

proof.text: The projection $\pi_A$ is a pullback of $q$, and $\pi_B$ is a pullback of $p$. They are fibrations by Step 2 and the conclusions of Step 1. Composing with $k$ shows $r,t\in F$. The graph factorization gives the exact equations $ri=\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal A}$ and $ti=v$. Since $i$, the identity, and $v$ belong to $W$, two-out-of-three in [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure] gives $r,t\in W$. Thus both $r$ and $t$ are trivial fibrations. Also $si=pri=p$, so $i$ is a map over $\mathcal S$.

source.place: Agent proof: two pullback projections, graph identities and two-out-of-three.

proof.text: Use the arbitrary $h:\mathcal R\to\mathcal S$ fixed in Step 1. Put $A_h=\mathcal R\times_{\mathcal S}\mathcal A$, $B_h=\mathcal R\times_{\mathcal S}\mathcal B$, and $Z_h=\mathcal R\times_{\mathcal S}Z$. Define $r_h(u,z)=(u,r(z))$, $t_h(u,z)=(u,t(z))$, $i_h(u,a)=(u,i(a))$ and $v_h(u,a)=(u,v(a))$ degree by degree. They commute with simplicial operators because all their coordinates do. The square for $r_h$ over $r$, with bottom map $A_h\to\mathcal A$, is a pullback: a simplex in its other pullback is a triple $((u,a),z)$ with $a=r(z)$ and $h(u)=p(a)$; deleting $a$ identifies it with $(u,z)\in Z_h$, since $p(r(z))=s(z)$. For $t_h$, the pullback of $t$ along $B_h\to\mathcal B$ consists in each degree of triples $((u,b),z)$ satisfying $b=t(z)$ and $h(u)=q(b)$. Deleting $b$ gives $(u,z)\in Z_h$ because $q(t(z))=s(z)$; the inverse sends $(u,z)$ to $((u,t(z)),z)$. Both identifications commute with simplicial operators, so this square is also an actual simplicial pullback. Step 2 and the lifting characterization of trivial fibrations in [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure] therefore show $r_h,t_h\in F\cap W$. No lifting condition on $h$ was used.

source.place: Agent proof: explicit iterated-pullback identification followed by trivial-fibration lifting.

proof.text: The coordinate formulas of Step 5 and the equations of Step 4 give $r_hi_h=\operatorname{id}_{A_h}$ and $t_hi_h=v_h$ as exact simplicial maps. Because $r_h\in W$ and the identity lies in $W$, two-out-of-three in [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure] gives $i_h\in W$. Since $t_h\in W$, two-out-of-three again gives $v_h\in W$. This proves a statement about the specified induced map itself, not just the existence of an equivalence between its source and target.

source.place: Agent proof: the two equations after base change and two applications of two-out-of-three.

proof.text: Finally, $A_h$ and $B_h$ are quasicategories. Indeed the projections $A_h\to\mathcal R$ and $B_h\to\mathcal R$ are pullbacks of $p$ and $q$, respectively, and hence lie in $F$ by Step 2. By [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure] the map $\mathcal R\to\Delta^0$ lies in $F$ because $\mathcal R$ is a quasicategory. Composition closure makes both terminal maps $A_h\to\Delta^0$ and $B_h\to\Delta^0$ fibrations, so that node’s fibrant-object characterization makes both pullbacks quasicategories. Clause (2) of [lem-coef-joyal-quasicategory-characterizations] now converts $v_h\in W$ from Step 6 into a functor equivalence in exactly the convention of the statement. The argument used neither $v\in F$ nor $h\in F$.

source.place: Theorem 3.6.1 and Corollary 3.6.6, after elementary closure of fibrations.
